reading.title: My Year
reading.text: There are twelve months in a year and I like them all for different reasons. In winter, from December to February, we have snow and I go skiing. In spring, from March to May, the flowers come out and the birds sing. Summer, from June to August, is hot, so we swim in the river. My birthday is in July. In autumn, from September to November, the leaves fall and it is cool. On Monday to Friday I go to school. At the weekend I play football with my friends. Every year in December our family goes to the mountains for a fortnight.

listening.title: Dates and Days
listening.script: There are three hundred and sixty five days in a year. A year which has three hundred and sixty six days is a leap year. There are twelve months in a year and seven days in a week. Saturday and Sunday are the weekend. Today is Tuesday. Yesterday was Monday. Tomorrow is Wednesday. Birds sing in the spring.

reading.title: Then and Now
reading.text: My grandfather often tells me about the past. He says that when he was young, people did not have television or computers. Then life was slow. Now we have phones and the internet. Grandfather was born in a small village. Then he moved to the city when he was twenty. He lives in Tashkent now. Last year he visited his old village for the first time in thirty years. He sees his brother three times a year. At the moment he is reading a book about the future. He thinks people may travel to Mars soon. I call him twice a week and see him once a month.

reading.title: Where Is Everybody?
reading.text: It was Saturday afternoon and I was at home. The house was quiet. My father was out at the shops. My mother was in the kitchen, making dinner. My sister was away on holiday, and my older brother was abroad. He studies in Germany. There were books and papers everywhere in my room, so I decided to tidy it. I put the books on the shelf and the papers in the bin. At the bottom of the bag, I found my old phone. At four o'clock, I met a friend at the station. We sat at the back of the bus and went to the cinema. It is on the left side of York Street.

reading.title: Two Drivers
reading.text: My father and my uncle both have cars, but they drive very differently. My father is a good driver. He drives slowly and carefully, and he never has accidents. He speaks quietly in the car and listens to soft music. My uncle is a bad driver. He drives fast and badly. His music is always too loud and he sings loudly. Last week he drove his car in the wrong direction. He is a friendly man, but he is sometimes unfriendly when he is driving. I like going with my father because it is calm and safe.

reading.title: Shopping for Dinner
reading.text: Mrs Aliyeva went to the market to buy some food for dinner. She bought a kilo of rice, three litres of milk and two loaves of bread. She also got some butter and sugar. The market was crowded and the traffic outside was terrible. A friendly man gave her some information about a cheaper shop. She also asked him for advice about fruit. He said, "Buy apples. They are fresh today." She bought five apples. When she got home, she was tired. She put the milk in the fridge and said, "Today I had some good news. We have a guest tonight!"
